characterization_methods.key_findings: at 1100 °C and 10 s^-1 the large deformation zone (zone 3) shows serrated grain boundaries with small equiaxed necklace-type DRX grains along the elongated original grain boundaries; zones 1 and 2 show larger, less recrystallized grains (Fig. 9(c))
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, prepared, ground, polished and etched with 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction); three deformation zones imaged (Fig. 9)
characterization_methods.purpose: to observe the microstructure evolution in the different deformation zones of the compressed sample
characterization_methods.technique: optical (laser confocal) microscopy of etched samples

characterization_methods.key_findings: peak stress of the 1100 °C, 10 s^-1 curve is above the 225 MPa level (Fig. 3(b))
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 1100 °C, ε̇ = 10 s^-1, maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92)
characterization_methods.purpose: to obtain the rheological (flow) stress curves and the hot-deformed specimens for microstructure analysis

analytical_models.equation_role: Z = ε̇ exp(Qp/RT) — temperature-compensated strain rate characterizing combined effect of T and strain rate
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ value for T = 1100 °C and ε̇ = 10 s^-1 is read from Table 1 (4th row, 1100 °C column). Qp is the average DRX activation energy over the whole experimental range (900–1150 °C, 0.01–10 s^-1).

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic sine constitutive analysis with the Zener-Hollomon parameter

analytical_models.equation_role: drex = a·d0^h·ε^p·ε̇^q·exp(Q/RT) + b ; fitted as drex = 807743.63 ε̇^-0.1903 exp(-120648.47/RT) + 4.338
analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model
analytical_models.model_note: Study-wide model fitted (Levenberg-Marquardt regression) to all compression conditions; initial grain size and strain taken as fixed. This sample (1100 °C, 10 s^-1) is one of the conditions covered by the model.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: billet set as a rigid plastic body and the die indenter as a rigid body; semi-symmetric specimen used as deformation model; contact interface friction set to shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient between billet and air set to 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C)
computational_details.simulation_method: finite element simulation coupled with regression analysis for DRX average grain size prediction
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% between predicted and experimental DRX average grain size; absolute error mostly within 3 µm

defect_interactions.interaction_type: necklace dynamic recrystallization nucleating at serrated elongated original grain boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: At 1100 °C and ε̇=10 s^-1, the grain boundaries of the large deformation zone are serrated and the small equiaxed DRX grains decorate the elongated original grain boundaries in a necklace arrangement (Fig. 9(c)).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The sample was heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s (first ramp of the compression schedule shown in Fig. 2).
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature 1100 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set temperature (1100 °C) before compression so the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was uniform.

Isothermal constant strain rate compression carried out on a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator at 1100 °C and a strain rate of 10 s^-1; maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricants applied to both end faces to reduce friction.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression on a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricants on both end faces; water-spray cooled after compression

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: true stress–true strain curve at T = 1100 °C and ε̇ = 10 s^-1 (Fig. 3(b)); the 10 s^-1 curve peaks above the 225 MPa level and then softens only slightly

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: serrated grain boundaries; small equiaxed necklace-type DRX grains distributed along the elongated original grain boundaries (Fig. 9(c))

microstructure_list.region: zone 3 – large deformation zone (core of the compressed sample)

structures.overall_structure: After 60% hot compression at 1100 °C and 10 s^-1, the degree of dynamic recrystallization varies with deformation zone: zone 3 (large deformation) > zone 2 (small deformation) > zone 1 (difficult deformation). In the large deformation zone (Fig. 9(c)) the grain boundaries are serrated and small equiaxed DRX grains are distributed along the elongated original grain boundaries in a small, equiaxed, necklace form; zones 1 and 2 retain larger, less recrystallized grains.

unmapped_findings: The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel, calculated from the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine equation (Eqs. 1-2) as an average over the whole experimental range (900–1150 °C, 0.01–10 s^-1), is 669.844 kJ mol^-1; the fitted slopes are k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690, and the stress level factor α = 0.00599.
Peak stress of this Fe-Mn-Al-C steel at 1100 °C and 10 s^-1 is above the 225 MPa level (Fig. 3(b)); the lnZ value for this condition is 60.98 (Table 1).

The dynamic recrystallization state diagram (Fig. 7) divides behaviour into area A (work hardening), area B (partial DRX) and area C (complete DRX) as functions of lnZ and strain; with increasing Z (increasing strain rate or decreasing T), the critical strain εc and steady-state strain εs of DRX both increase.

From combining microstructure observation and DRX average grain size, the paper concludes that fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working in the ranges 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1; the present sample (1100 °C, 10 s^-1) falls in the latter range.
The DRX average grain size prediction model established with DEFORM-3D and the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm is drex = 807743.63 ε̇^-0.1903 exp(-120648.47/RT) + 4.338, with R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%.
